The earlier in the month you stake, the more you collect

Your stake is averaged across the whole month. Cover your slice from day one and you collect your full share; cover it from the middle of the month and you collect about half. A large balance held for a few days counts only for those days.

How staking works & what it costs

Why stake

Every month, 20% of all platform fees collected go back to the people who generated them, split in proportion to each wallet's fees: the NQV8 fees it paid, plus its credited share of the USDC fee on bounties (poster and builder) and creator memberships (member and creator). Only wallets with fees that month earn a share. Staking decides how much of your share you collect: cover your slice and you collect all of it, cover half and you collect half. Whatever is not collected rolls into the next month's pool.

How much you need

The platform aims to have a set share of all circulating NQV8 staked: 10% today, rising toward 30% as more of the supply reaches circulation. Your slice of that target equals your slice of the month's fees. Pay 5% of the fees and your slice is 5% of the target. Staking more than your slice earns nothing extra. The figure at the top of this card is your slice so far this month, read live from the contract; it moves as other wallets pay fees and is fixed when the month closes.

Unstaking takes 30 days

Requesting an unstake starts a 30-day cooldown, and the amount stops counting toward rewards immediately — including for the month in progress. Changed your mind? Cancel & restake puts the whole amount back with no wait. The 30 days matches the reward period, so collecting every month means staying staked.

Rewards are claimed, not sent

Nothing arrives automatically. When a month closes it appears under Claimable Rewards above with your share and a Claim button. There is no deadline — a claim you have earned stays claimable indefinitely, so you can leave it sitting as long as you like. Each month shows your slice and how much of it your stake covered.

What "locked in bonds" means

A bond is staked NQV8 held behind a bid or an accepted job. It is returned in full if you are not chosen, withdraw, or deliver on time, and part of it can be burned if you win the job and then default. Bonded NQV8 cannot be unstaked until that commitment is settled, and it counts toward your slice for every day it is locked.

Staking is non-custodial. Your NQV8 sits in the staking contract, which cannot pay it anywhere but back to you, and the contract's recovery function is barred from touching staked funds.

Claimable Rewards

Closed months are claimed, not paid out automatically. How much of each you collect depends on how well your stake covered your slice that month.

Rule 144-Inspired Sale Limits — Enforced On-Chain

The founder's entire NQV8 allocation is held in a dedicated lockup smart contract. Tokens can only leave via the sell() function, which enforces a rolling 1%-of-circulating-supply cap per 90-day window — modeled on SEC Rule 144 insider volume discipline. Sales exceeding the limit are rejected by the contract, not just policy. This is a voluntary, self-imposed commitment mechanism.

Sale Limit Per 3-Month Period

  • •1% of circulating supply in any rolling 3-month period

About NQVate

Everything you need to know about the platform and how to get started.

NQV8

The complete startup platform — on-chain.

NQVate gives founders everything they need to build, fund, and grow a startup in one place — a talent marketplace, tokenized equity, on-chain escrow, investor tools, and AI-powered assistance. Built on Ethereum.

Built on Arbitrum On-chain equity AI-powered NQV8 token

What is NQVate?

NQVate is the operating system for early-stage startups. It replaces the fragmented stack of cap table software, payroll tools, escrow services, and investor portals that founders cobble together in year one — with a single platform where every tool works together and every transaction settles on-chain.

Unlike traditional platforms, NQVate lets founders offer real equity stakes in their companies as compensation, lets builders earn ownership in the projects they help build, and lets investors buy and sell those stakes on an integrated exchange — all without lawyers, paperwork, or gatekeepers.

Why build your startup on-chain?

Most startups spend their first months stitching together a cap table spreadsheet, a separate payments processor, contractor agreements, and a half dozen disconnected tools just to track who owns what and who's been paid. NQVate replaces all of that with financial infrastructure that's built into your project from day one.

📊

Your cap table maintains itself

Every time someone earns equity completing a bounty or buys a stake on the exchange, it's recorded automatically on-chain. No spreadsheets to update, no version control disputes about who has the latest cap table — it's always live and always accurate.

💸

Payments and escrow are built in

No separate payroll system, no chasing invoices, no wire transfer delays. Funds are locked in escrow the moment you accept a bid and released automatically when work is approved — the financial plumbing most startups spend months setting up is just... there.

🌍

Hire and pay anyone, anywhere

No international wire fees, no waiting days for cross-border payments, no separate contractor agreements per country. A builder in Manila gets paid exactly as fast as one in Manhattan — settlement is instant and identical everywhere.

🔍

Built-in trust for investors

Anyone you raise from can independently verify your cap table, trade history, and equity structure on Arbiscan — no data room, no trust-me spreadsheet. Transparency is the default, not something you have to set up.

💡 This is the replacement, not a stopgap

Cap table software, payroll providers, cross-border payment processors, escrow services — these are all separate companies charging separate fees to solve problems that shouldn't exist in the first place. NQVate replaces that entire stack with infrastructure that's faster, cheaper, transparent by default, and works identically for every founder, builder, and investor on the platform, anywhere in the world.

What can you do on NQVate?

🔨

Marketplace — Post & Bid on Work

The heart of NQVate. Post tasks you need done, or bid on tasks others have posted.

🔨 Build Requests (Bounties)

Post a specific task — a smart contract, a UI component, a logo, anything. Set your compensation in USDC, equity, or a combination. Builders browse and bid. You review bids and accept the best one. Funds are locked in escrow automatically and released when you approve the work.

Example posting:

Build a Solidity staking contract

Compensation: $2,500 USDC · Category: Blockchain

✅ Funds locked in escrow on acceptance

💰 Funding Requests

Seeking investment for your project? Post a funding request outlining what you're raising and what you're offering. Investors browse and submit funding proposals. Equity terms are locked on-chain when accepted, giving investors a permanent, verifiable ownership stake.

Example posting:

Raising $50,000 USDC — 10% equity

For: AI SaaS product · Verified LLC

📈 Equity registered on Arbitrum

💡 How escrow works

When you accept a bid, the agreed payment is automatically locked in the NQVate Escrow smart contract on Arbitrum. The builder does the work, submits it, and you review it. If you approve — funds release instantly to the builder. If you don't respond within 7 days of a submission, they release to the builder automatically; if the deadline passes with nothing submitted, your escrow is refunded. If there's a dispute, Claude AI acts as the arbitrator and splits funds fairly. No humans, no delays. NQVate never holds the money — it sits in the contract.

🔒 Builders stake a refundable bond to bid

To place a bid, a builder stakes NQV8 as a delivery commitment — 10–25% of the posting's value depending on its scope, with a 100 NQV8 minimum and a 500,000 NQV8 maximum. It comes straight back if you aren't chosen, you withdraw your bid, or the posting is cancelled, and it is returned in full when you win and deliver. Part of it can be forfeited only if you win and then miss the deadline or lose a dispute. Whatever is forfeited is burned — neither the founder nor NQVate receives it.

📈

Equity Exchange

Buy and sell ownership stakes in projects — all on-chain.

Every equity stake earned through bounty completion or investment is tokenized on the NQVate Equity Registry smart contract. Stake holders can list their equity for sale on the exchange, and buyers can purchase at the asking price or make counter-offers — all settled in USDC directly on-chain.

🎙️

Podcasts & Streams

Publish episodes, go live, and build a paying audience.

Posting an episode or going live costs 1 NQV8, the same as any other post, and the same content rules apply. Creators can offer a paid 30-day membership in USDC for subscribers-only episodes and streams. The member pays the creator wallet to wallet — 96.5% to the creator and a 3.5% platform fee — and NQVate never holds the money. Creators and their members both earn a share of the monthly rewards from that fee.

🪙

NQV8 Token

The native utility token powering the platform.

NQV8 is used for all platform fees — posting bounties, submitting bids, verifying your entity, generating AI flow maps, and more. Fees are fixed in NQV8 (most actions cost 1–500 NQV8), so they do not change when the token price does.

Every month, 20% of all platform fees go back to the people who generated them: the NQV8 fees you paid, plus your share of the USDC fee on bounties you posted or completed and on memberships you bought or sold. Getting Started on NQVate

New to Web3? No problem. Follow these steps and you'll be up and running in under 15 minutes. We'll explain everything — including the crypto parts — in plain English.

1

Create your NQVate account

Click Create Account in the top right. You'll need:

✓

A username

Your public identity on NQVate. Choose something you're happy to be known by — it's shown on all your posts and bids.

✓

An email and password

Used to log in. Your email is private — it's never shown publicly.

✓

A connected wallet (required)

This is where your NQV8 tokens, USDC payments, and equity stakes will live. Don't worry — we'll walk you through setting one up in the next step.

🎁 Signup bonus

Every new account gets 1,000 NQV8 (worth $10 at the $0.01 peg) claimed directly to your wallet — enough for your first postings, posts and comments, and to cover the refundable stake on a small bounty bid.

2

Set up a crypto wallet

A wallet is like a bank account for crypto — it holds your tokens and signs transactions. You need one to use NQVate. MetaMask is the most popular and easiest to set up; Coinbase Wallet and any WalletConnect-compatible wallet work too.

Setting up MetaMask (5 minutes)

  1. 1 Go to metamask.io/download and install the browser extension (Chrome, Firefox, or Brave).
  2. 2 Click Create a new wallet and follow the prompts to set a password.
  3. 3 ⚠️ Write down your Secret Recovery Phrase and store it somewhere safe offline. This is the only way to recover your wallet if you lose access. Never share it with anyone — ever.
  4. 4 Your wallet is ready. You'll see an address like 0x1234...abcd — this is your public address, safe to share.

On mobile?

Download the MetaMask app from the App Store or Google Play. You can also use WalletConnect to connect any mobile wallet — tap "Connect Wallet" on NQVate and select WalletConnect to scan a QR code.

3

Connect your wallet — Arbitrum is set up for you

NQVate runs on Arbitrum One — a fast, cheap network built on Ethereum. There is nothing to configure: most wallets already include Arbitrum, and when you connect, NQVate asks your wallet to switch to it — and adds it for you if it is missing. Just approve the prompt.

Wallet didn't switch? Add Arbitrum manually ▾
  1. 1 Open the network list in your wallet and choose Arbitrum One if it is there.
  2. 2 If it is not, go to chainlist.org/chain/42161 and add it from there, or add a custom network with these details:
Network NameArbitrum One
RPC URLhttps://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc
Chain ID42161
SymbolETH
Explorerhttps://arbiscan.io

💡 Why Arbitrum?

Arbitrum is built on top of Ethereum but transactions cost a fraction of a cent (vs. $5–$50 on Ethereum mainnet). This makes small actions like posting bids or paying platform fees practical. Your assets are just as secure — Arbitrum settles everything back to Ethereum.

4

Get ETH for gas fees

Every transaction on the blockchain costs a tiny fee called "gas" — paid in ETH. On Arbitrum, gas fees are very small (usually under $0.05), but you need a small amount of ETH in your wallet to pay them.

Two ways to get ETH on Arbitrum:

Option A — Buy directly on Arbitrum (easiest)

Use Coinbase, Kraken, or Binance to buy ETH and withdraw directly to Arbitrum One. When withdrawing, select Arbitrum as the network. You only need $5–$10 worth of ETH for gas.

Option B — Bridge from Ethereum mainnet

If you already have ETH on Ethereum mainnet, use the official Arbitrum Bridge to move it to Arbitrum. Connect your wallet, enter the amount, and confirm. Takes ~10 minutes. Note: the bridge transaction itself costs Ethereum gas, so only worth it if you're moving more than ~$50.

⚠️ How much ETH do I need?

For normal NQVate usage, $2–$5 worth of ETH will last you a very long time. Each NQVate action uses roughly $0.01–$0.05 in gas. You won't need to top up often.

5

Claim your free NQV8 and start exploring

Once your wallet is connected and you have a little ETH for gas, claim your 1,000 NQV8 signup bonus from your Profile page. Then you're ready to go — the NQVerse is your home screen, with the feed, rankings, listings and chat beside the map.

6

Getting USDC for payments (optional but useful)

Most bounties on NQVate are paid in USDC — a stablecoin always worth $1.00. If you're posting bounties or joining a creator's membership, you'll need USDC on Arbitrum.

Getting USDC on Arbitrum:

  1. 1 Buy USDC on Coinbase or any major exchange.
  2. 2 When withdrawing, select Arbitrum One as the network and paste your wallet address. The USDC will arrive in your wallet within a few minutes.
  3. 3 Alternatively, use Uniswap on Arbitrum to swap ETH for USDC directly in your wallet.

Common Questions

Do I need crypto experience to use NQVate? ▾

No. The guide above covers everything from scratch. The only crypto-specific things you need are a wallet and a small amount of ETH for gas fees. Everything else — posting, bidding, chatting — works like any other web platform.

What if I lose my wallet? ▾

Your wallet can be recovered using your 12-word Secret Recovery Phrase (also called a seed phrase). This is why it's critical to write it down and store it safely offline when you first create your wallet. If you lose both your device and your seed phrase, the wallet cannot be recovered — no one can help you, not even MetaMask or NQVate.

Is my NQVate account tied to my wallet? ▾

Yes, but you can change your connected wallet from your Profile → Settings at any time. Your NQVate account (username, profile, posts) lives in our database. Your tokens and equity stakes live on the blockchain in your wallet. Changing your wallet updates where future payments and rewards are sent.

What is equity on NQVate? Is it legally binding? ▾

NQVate equity is tokenized ownership recorded on the Arbitrum blockchain via the NQVate Equity Registry smart contract. It represents a stake in a project, registered on-chain against a verified entity. However, NQVate is not a broker, legal advisor, or party to any equity transaction. The on-chain record is a transparent, immutable ledger entry — but the legal enforceability of equity stakes depends on the agreements between the parties involved. For significant transactions, consult a lawyer.

What happens if there's a dispute? ▾

Either party can file a dispute for 1,000 NQV8. Claude AI immediately reviews the project description, the accepted bid, all submitted deliverables, and any evidence provided by both parties. Claude issues a binding ruling, splitting the escrow funds proportionally — typically within minutes. There is no appeals process and NQVate is not involved. This keeps things fast and unbiased. A ruling also settles the builder's bid bond: nothing is forfeited if the builder is awarded 75% or more, and a larger part is forfeited the less of the work was delivered.
